The season ran from 15 February to 6 November 2004. [[Atlético Sport Aviação|ASA]] were the defending champions. The league comprised 14 teams, the bottom three of which were relegated to the 2005 [[Gira Angola]]. [[Atlético Sport Aviação|ASA]] were crowned champions, winning a third title in a row, while [[Académica Petróleo Kwanda Soyo|Académica do Soyo]], [[S.L. Benfica (Lubango)|Benfica do Lubango]] and [[F.C. Bravos do Maquis|Bravos do Maquis]], the three clubs that were promoted that same season, were relegated.{{cite web |url=http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/en_us/noticias/desporto/2006/9/41/Agosto-New-National-Champions,69cf1de3-1264-4d84-afa5-5984c6d4b8e3.html |title=1º de Agosto New National Champions |publisher=ANGOP.com |date=15 Oct 2006 |access-date=14 Dec 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304045409/http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/en_us/noticias/desporto/2006/9/41/Agosto-New-National-Champions,69cf1de3-1264-4d84-afa5-5984c6d4b8e3.html |url-status=dead }} [[Love (footballer)|Arsénio Kabungula]] aka ''Love'' of [[Atlético Sport Aviação|ASA]] finished as the top scorer with 17 goals.{{cite web |url=http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/pt_pt/noticias/desporto/2004/10/46/Futebol-Love-sagrou-melhor-marcador-Girabola-2004,ac8d663e-7785-4fb6-ae64-98316f9f2f35.html |title=Futebol: Love sagrou-se melhor marcador do Girabola 2004 |publisher=ANGOP.com |date=8 Nov 2004 |access-date=13 Sep 2015}} ==Changes from the 2004 season== '''Relegated:''' [[S.L.
